A Bloomberg report yesterday suggested that the future Apple Watch lineup could see a significant shake-up.

It specifically mentioned that Apple is exploring the possibility of launching one or more models with a round face design instead of a square one…

Most smartwatches are round

Although square-faced watches have existed for over a hundred years, most traditional watches are round, and the same applies to Android smartwatches. Examples include:

  • Amazfit Active Max
  • Samsung Galaxy Watch 9
  • Motorola Moto Watch
  • All Garmin models (Venu, Epix Pro, Forerunner, Fenix)
  • Google Pixel Watch

Apple's choice of a rectangular design is the outlier, so it wouldn't be surprising for the company to consider launching a round Apple Watch in the future.

There is a case for a round Apple Watch

The reason Apple originally chose a rectangular design is that it can display more information. This is no accident — every other screen we use daily, whether phones, tablets, laptops, monitors, and so on, is rectangular.

Ultimately, this is a trade-off between aesthetics and practicality. There will always be those who prioritise practicality, so the rectangular Apple Watch design will undoubtedly continue to exist. But there are also plenty of people who place great importance on appearance, and many genuinely have a strong preference for round designs when it comes to both traditional and smartwatches.

Furthermore, not everyone who wears an Apple Watch needs to display a large amount of information on the face. Even if you don't frequently check the screen, there are still plenty of good reasons to wear an Apple Watch. For example:

  • Health and fitness monitoring
  • Sleep tracking
  • Emergency features, such as fall detection
  • Contactless payment

Of the above, health and fitness monitoring is the primary reason for many people; if you mainly don't use your Apple Watch as a content device, then a round screen would actually work perfectly fine for you.

But the case for an Apple Ring is even stronger

However, if you're the type of user who primarily uses an Apple Watch for health and fitness monitoring, and basically never uses it to check information, then I believe a smart ring would be the more… sensible choice.

I personally switched from the Apple Watch to the Oura smart ring back in 2024, and have recently upgraded to the fifth-generation model. I love how understated it is, allowing me to wear my favourite traditional watch, and it only needs charging once a week.

Almost two years ago to the day, I stated that the smart ring had successfully replaced the Apple Watch as my favourite, and that Apple should launch a similar product. My view hasn't changed since, and Gurman notes that Eddy Cue is also a staunch supporter of the smart ring, making it seem like a matter of course.

I do think it's possible that Apple will release a round Apple Watch model, but I'm even more looking forward to seeing an Apple Ring come to fruition. What do you think? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments.
